messages.subject: Warning related with psi matrix
messages.body_plain:
Hello.

I am trying to fit a sem model with blavaan. Everything appears to work, but the following warning appears:

Warning: blavaan WARNING: As specified, the psi covariance matrix is neither diagonal nor unrestricted, so the actual prior might differ from the stated prior. See https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08667

I read the referenced paper and I would like to test the third solution suggested (Combining LKJ with Informative Priors), the one explained here: http://srmart.in/informative-priors-for-correlation-matrices-an-easy-approach/

Is it possible to implement this solution in blavaan or it is necessary to implement it directly in Stan?

messages.subject: Re: Warning related with psi matrix
messages.body_plain:
Armel,

I hope to make future progress in blavaan here, but it is not automatically available at the moment.

To implement that solution, one possibility is to export blavaan's Stan file using mcmcfile = TRUE, then edit the priors (around line 925). I could provide more input if needed, but many people shy away from that Stan file because it is written for general SEM, so takes some time to get oriented.

On the other hand, unless you are doing something with Bayes factors or with prior predictive distributions, you might be able to safely ignore the warning.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Hello.

I am trying to generate samples from the prior distributions of this model:

model <- "
  # Latent variable definitions
  Alt =~ no_overlap_mixed_0_65 + no_overlap_mixed_1_7 + overlap_mixed_0_65 +
  overlap_mixed_1_7
  Inh =~ no_overlap_red_0_65 + no_overlap_red_1_7 + overlap_red_0_65 +
  overlap_red_1_7
  Act =~ black_arrows_pc + red_arrows_pc + mixed_arrows_pc
  IF =~ T1 + T2 + T3 + T4
  HV =~ CV1A + CV1B + CV1C + CV1D + IG11A + IG11B + CT + VL17A + VL17B + VL17C
  PO =~ gaze_duration_DF + regression_path_duration_DF + total_duration_DF

  # Regressions
  PO ~ IF + HV + Alt + Act + Inh
  HV ~ IF + Act
  IF ~ Alt + Inh + Act
  Act ~ Alt + Inh

  # Residual correlation
  Alt ~~ Inh
"

When I run

priorSamples <- bsem(model, data = data, std.lv <http://std.lv> = T, std.ov = T, prisamp = TRUE)

I get the error

Error in eval(mc, parent.frame()) :
  Exception: mismatch in dimension declared and found in context; processing stage=data initialization; variable name=YXbar; position=0; dims declared=(5,28); dims found=(1,28)  (in 'model_stanmarg' at line 284)

failed to create the sampler; sampling not done
Stan model 'stanmarg' does not contain samples.
Error in rowvec[samppar] <- grep(stanvec[j], names(b.est)) :
  replacement has length zero

How can I fix this error? I am using blavaan_0.4-7

messages.subject: Re: Error with prisamp = TRUE
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the report. Here are two questions:

1. Can you estimate the model with prisamp = FALSE? (the usual model estimation)

2. Do you have missing data? If so, maybe try creating a copy of your dataset, except with all the NA values filled in with a number, e.g.,

data[is.na <http://is.na>(data)] <- 0

If #2 works, there might be a bug. But it doesn't matter what is in your dataset when prisamp=TRUE, so it would be safe to fill in the missing data.

Ed

messages.subject: Prior for covariance between latent variables
messages.subject_clean: Prior for covariance between latent variables
messages.body_plain:
Hello.

I am trying to fit a structural model with a covariance between two factors. I am using the default beta(1,1) prior for rho.

I think that the rho prior distribution should look like hist(rbeta(1e6, 1, 1)), but when I run

fit <- bsem(model, data = data, prisamp = T)
plot(fit, plot.type = "hist", pars = 41) # paramater 41 is a covariance between two factors

I obtain a plot similar to hist(rbeta(1e6, 0.3, 0.3)).

I apologize if this a misunderstanding of how probability distributions work, but I think that the plot of the prior samples imply that correlations extremely negative and extremely positive are more probable than any other values.

Is there a way in blavaan to set a prior such that positive correlations are much more likely than extremely negative or near zero correlations?

messages.subject: Re: Prior for covariance between latent variables
messages.subject_clean: Prior for covariance between latent variables
messages.body_plain:
Could you send the code for the full model? This is possibly a case of "opaque" priors related to the recent paper that I posted here:

https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08667

See the "positive definite constraints" section. But the U-shaped distribution that you describe is unexpected; it is usually the reverse.

For specifying that positive correlations are more likely, the first beta parameter should be larger than the second. For example, beta(30,20) might be fairly reasonable:

-1 + 2 * rbeta(1e6, 30, 20)

messages.subject_clean: Prior for covariance between latent variables
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the code. I found a bug where, for your model, the posterior distribution is still estimated even though prisamp = TRUE. To work around it, add

meanstructure = TRUE

to your bsem command. The bug is also fixed on github.

Also, the warning about "the actual prior might differ from the stated prior" does not apply to your model. You could safely use any beta prior for the single free correlation. If you wanted something other than beta(30, 20), I would recommend to look at various histograms of random numbers from beta distributions, e.g.,

hist(-1 + 2 * rbeta(1e5, 40, 25))

until you find some suitable beta parameters.

Ed

messages.body_plain:
Sorry again for the delay and thanks for digging into this problem. I agree with your assessment, and the bug should be fixed on github.

On Fri, 2023-02-24 at 13:22 -0500, Brad Cosentino wrote:

> Thank you very much, Ed. I took your suggestion and standardized the data, then refit the model using blavaan (via targets = stan and JAGS) and the JAGS model file written by blavaan (via the jagsUI package). A few follow-up points:
>
> 1) With the exception of the issue with variances being off by a row, the blavaan estimates with targets = stan and jags are pretty consistent with the lavaan output, with good convergence. So standardization helped a lot in JAGs, even using the default prior options in blavaan.
>
> 2) When I fit the model using the JAGS file written by blavaan (using the same MCMC parameters and priors as blavaan), the parameter estimates are not consistent with those from blavaan or lavaan, and there are significant convergence issues.
>
> 3) I think I tracked down the issue in the JAGS file output from blavaan. The parameter being set to 1000 is psi[1,1,1], but I don't think that's a precision. It looks like the psi parameters are variances for the latent variables (e.g., eta[i, 1] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,1], 1/psi[3,3,g[i]]). The quantity 1/psi in the code is set as the precision, so psi must be the variance (precision = 1/variance). So I don't think it's correct to set the variance to 1000. The variance term should be constrained to something like 0.001. However, I don't think psi is the correct variance parameter to constrain in this case, as it's the error variance for an endogenous latent variable. Instead, I think the correct parameter to constrain is alpha[1,1,1], which corresponds to the error variance for the observed indicator "abu", which is the only indicator for the latent variable "abundance". I modified the JAGS code to make those changes, and the output was qualitatively similar to the blavaan output and lavaan output, and with very good convergence.
>
> Below I've pasted a comparison of the estimates from the various model fits, as well is the original JAGS code produced by blavaan and the version that I modified. It's strange that blavaan reports seemingly correct parameter estimates with solid convergence when target = jags, whereas using the JAGS file output seems to produce very different estimates with poor convergence. Perhaps an issue with how the JAGS file output is being written. In any case, I'm encouraged that the modifications I made to the JAGS file seem to work, but please let me know if you see any issues with the changes I made.
>
> Many thanks,
> Brad
>
>
> ########JAGS FILE PRODUCED BY BLAVAAN#########
> I flagged where I think corrections are needed.
>
> model {
>   for(i in 1:N) {
>     abu[i] ~ dnorm(mu[i,1], 1/theta[1,1,g[i]])  #theta variance should be constrained

It looks like the psi parameters are variances for the latent variables (e.g., eta[i, 1] ~ dnorm(mu_eta[i,1], 1/psi[3,3,g[i]]). The quantity 1/psi in the code is set as the precision, so psi must be the variance (precision = 1/variance). So I don't think it's correct to set the variance to 1000. The variance term should be constrained to something like 0.001. However, I don't think psi is the correct variance parameter to constrain in this case, as it's the error variance for an endogenous latent variable. Instead, I think the correct parameter to constrain is alpha[1,1,1], which corresponds to the error variance for the observed indicator "abu", which is the only indicator for the latent variable "abundance". messages.subject: NA MargLogLik and low BGammaHat
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am fitting Bayesian RI-CLPMs with two variables (Enj, Eff, measured at 13 timepoints), two covariates (preTest, preEnj, measured at the beginning), two outcomes (postTest, game, measured at the end), and two dummy variables (3 groups: group0 is the reference of group1 and group2). The main research question is whether there are group differences on Enj, Eff, preTest, and game.

Some issues:
1.  MargLogLik value is NA. What does this mean and how should I proceed?
2.  BGammaHat .865, which is below .900, is quite different from BCFI .918. What could be the reason? How to increase the model fit?
3. When looking at the output, are there any other things that I need to worry?

fit.RICLPMpoCogEnjEff <- '
# mediator
RIEnj ~ a1*group1 + a2*group2

# direct Effect
RIEff ~ c11*group1 + c12*group2
postTest ~ c21*group1 + c22*group2
game ~ c31*group1 + c32*group2

# add group (use group0 as reference)
preTest ~ f1*group1 + f2*group2
preEnj ~ e1*group1 + e2*group2

# add outcomes z2
# Residual variance and covariance z2
postTest ~~ postTest
game ~~ game
game ~~ postTest

# add regression
postTest ~ preTest
game ~ preTest

# add covariates z1
# 1b) Regression of random intercepts on time-invariant predictor z1
RIEnj ~ preEnj
RIEff ~ preTest

# Residual variance and covariance z1
preEnj ~~ preEnj
preTest ~~ preTest

messages.body_plain:
Yuan

some models with high number of constraints end up with issues of NA on on the margloglik, but this is not a problem in practice as it is only needed for bayes factor calculations (which I dont recommend)

About the gamma hat, remember that the cutoff of 0.9 is arbitrary and there is no reason to belief ot applies to all models/data, etc.

You can look at modification indices, but guven that you dont have an actual measurement model, might indicate to relase model constraints that could go agaiants the restrictions for theis model.

Another note, you dont need to save so many samples (1500 per chain), could probably do with 500

You can estimate posterior modifiction indices with this code and the ppmc function

### modification indices
discFUN <- list(mod.ind_mi = function(object){
  temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
  mods <- temp$mi
  names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
  return(mods)
},mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
  temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
  sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
  names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
  return(sepc.all )
}
)

#######
## PPMC - Modification indices
#######
out <- ppmc(bfit, thin=5, discFUN = discFUN)

### -MI
ss_mod_mi <- summary(out, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi", sort.by <http://sort.by>="Median", decreasing=T)[1:5,]
### -SEPC
ss_mod_sepc <- summary(out, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all", sort.by <http://sort.by>="Median", decreasing=T)[1:5,]

messages.body_plain:
Thank you Mauricio!

Sample:
1). When sample = 500, I got below warnings so I increased sample =1500. I was planning to use sample =10000 (which takes 40 mins each run) in the final reporting. Perhaps no need to be so high?
3: Bulk Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior means and medians may be unreliable.
Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#bulk-ess
4: Tail Effective Samples Size (ESS) is too low, indicating posterior variances and tail quantiles may be unreliable.
Running the chains for more iterations may help. See
https://mc-stan.org/misc/warnings.html#tail-ess

2) When sample = 1500, I also got below warning. I checked suggestions in this group, it seems that  I can ignore this warning?
blavaan WARNING: As specified, the psi covariance matrix is neither diagonal nor unrestricted, so the actual prior might differ from the stated prior. See
 https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.08667

Modification indices:
1)In the code that you shared, I replaced "bfit" with my model "fit.RICLPMpoCogEnjEff". It's almost 2 hours, but the analysis is still running and nothing comes out... Did I do anything wrong?

Best,
Yuan

> Yuan
>
> some models with high number of constraints end up with issues of NA on on the margloglik, but this is not a problem in practice as it is only needed for bayes factor calculations (which I dont recommend)
>
> About the gamma hat, remember that the cutoff of 0.9 is arbitrary and there is no reason to belief ot applies to all models/data, etc.
>
> You can look at modification indices, but guven that you dont have an actual measurement model, might indicate to relase model constraints that could go agaiants the restrictions for theis model.
>
> Another note, you dont need to save so many samples (1500 per chain), could probably do with 500
>
> You can estimate posterior modifiction indices with this code and the ppmc function
>
> ### modification indices
> discFUN <- list(mod.ind_mi = function(object){
>   temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
>   mods <- temp$mi
>   names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
>   return(mods)
> },mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
>   temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
>   sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
>   names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
>   return(sepc.all )
> }
> )
>
> #######
> ## PPMC - Modification indices
> #######
> out <- ppmc(bfit, thin=5, discFUN = discFUN)
>
> ### -MI
> ss_mod_mi <- summary(out, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_mi", sort.by <http://sort.by>="Median", decreasing=T)[1:5,]
> ### -SEPC
> ss_mod_sepc <- summary(out, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all", sort.by <http://sort.by>="Median", decreasing=T)[1:5,]

messages.subject: Re: NA MargLogLik and low BGammaHat
messages.body_plain:
Yuan

1. 10000 is an overkill, if 1500 is enough to not get the ESS warnings you are fine. It would only be neccesary to have sucha a large sample for bayes factor estabilibility. But not for inferences etc

2. Yes, that is a warning not a problematic error

3. Sadly, that is a know problem with modification indices, they can take a while for large models, as it is estimating the lavaan indices 600 time for example. If R is still running I would let it run a for a bot. or you can increase thin so that it estimates it less times

out <- ppmc( fit.RICLPMpoCogEnjEff , thin=8, discFUN = discFUN)

as a last resort, you can run the model with lavaan and use its modification indices. They should not point to different parameters. Honetsly I am not sure what would be recommended as added parameters in this model with so many constraints

> > some models with high number of constraints end up with issues of NA on on the margloglik, but this is not a problem in practice as it is only needed for bayes factor calculations (which I dont recommend)
> >
> > About the gamma hat, remember that the cutoff of 0.9 is arbitrary and there is no reason to belief ot applies to all models/data, etc.
> >
> > You can look at modification indices, but guven that you dont have an actual measurement model, might indicate to relase model constraints that could go agaiants the restrictions for theis model.
> >
> > Another note, you dont need to save so many samples (1500 per chain), could probably do with 500
> >
> > You can estimate posterior modifiction indices with this code and the ppmc function
> >
> > ### modification indices
> > discFUN <- list(mod.ind_mi = function(object){
> >   temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
> >   mods <- temp$mi
> >   names(mods) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
> >   return(mods)
> > },mod.ind_sepc.all = function(object){
> >   temp <- modificationindices(object,free.remove = F)
> >   sepc.all <- temp$sepc.all
> >   names(sepc.all) <- paste0(temp$lhs,temp$op,temp$rhs)
> >   return(sepc.all )
> > }
> > )
> >
> > #######
> > ## PPMC - Modification indices
> > #######
> > out <- ppmc(bfit, thin=5, discFUN = discFUN)

> > ### -SEPC
> > ss_mod_sepc <- summary(out, prob=.9, discFUN = "mod.ind_sepc.all", sort.by <http://sort.by>="Median", decreasing=T)[1:5,]

messages.subject: blavaan do.fit argument not behaving as (I) expected
messages.subject_clean: blavaan do.fit argument not behaving as (I) expected
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to deal with one problem in blavaan for which I want to use the do.fit argument, but it is not behaving as expected, or at least not as I expected.

There is something wrong with my data so that if I try to use bcfa I get the following error:

Error in eigen(VarCov, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE) :
  infinite or missing values in 'x'

If I am working with lavaan instead of blavaan, I don't get an error, but instead when I call summary I get the following warning:

lavaan 0.6.15 did not run (perhaps do.fit = FALSE)?
** WARNING ** Estimates below are simply the starting values

However, I am confused by how lavaan and blavaan behave differently when I try to run them on this bad data and use the do.fit argument. When I run lavaan with do.fit = FALSE, I get a fit object in my working environment. When I use blavaan with do.fit = FALSE, it appears that it's still trying to estimate the model, since I get the previous error with the eigenvalues I posted above. I do not get a fit object in my working environment. More importantly, i don't see the lavExport folder in my working directory. I just want to grab this bad data in the format in which it would be passed to Stan. How could I achieve this?

Please note that this question is not about why am I getting the error with my data or how can it be fixed. This question is about how to "force" blavaan to give me a data object even though that there is something wrong with the data. I think that should be possible, right? Since I am not asking it to perform estimation but just to reshape my data from the data frame format to the list format needed for Stan.
